newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Cullen moots changes to pension question.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Cullen moots changes to pension question.

text.p: Parliament's Finance and Expenditure select committee is likely to rewrite the question due to be put to voters in a referendum on compulsory superannuation, Labour's finance spokesman said on Tuesday.

"(Treasurer Winston) Peters has drafted a biased referendum question which doesn't even mention the word compulsory. The signs are that the select committee will resist that, rewriting it to give an honest reflection of what the scheme is about," Michael Cullen said.
He said Labour would be drafting amendments to that effect. The draft legislation would see the referendum ask voters, "Are you for or against the retirement savings scheme?".
Details of the scheme are being developed by a group of government and private sector representatives.

Cullen welcomed recent indications from at least three government backbenchers that they would vote against legislation to enforce compulsory superannuation if the turnout at September's postal referendum was too low.

The coalition agreement between the conservative National Party and nationalist New Zealand First allows government MPs to argue for or against the scheme, but binds them to support the implementation of the law if there is a positive result.
